turns.t: Okay, so my sore throat is back again. It's like the fourth time since winter, and I'm honestly sick of it.
Four times. That's a pattern worth chasing. When did this round start?
Um, a couple of weeks ago, I guess. But it's been on and off for about two months, if you count the earlier ones.
So two months of it coming and going, with this stretch being the latest. What does it feel like?
Kind of scratchy, like I swallowed a handful of gravel. Worse when I first wake up.
Gravel, got it. Anything else going on, besides the throat?
There's these lumps under my jaw. They feel like little peas, right here, on both sides.
Those are lymph glands. Think of them as the guard posts on the road into your head, they swell up when there's trouble in the neighborhood.
Huh. That makes sense, actually.
Have you had a fever with this?
Yeah, last week I had one, I was kind of shivery for a couple days. But that went away on Sunday.
Good. Fever gone, then. Any cough with it?
No, not really. Just the throat.
And is swallowing hard, like food getting stuck?
No, it hurts a little, but nothing gets stuck.
Okay. Let's talk about what you're taking. What's in your medicine cabinet right now?
There's my blood pressure pill, lisinopril, 10 mg, once a day. I take it with my coffee.
Great. Anything else, even stuff from the drugstore?
Tylenol, 500 mg, when it's bad. Probably most days, honestly. And those throat lozenges, I get through a few a day.
Okay. That's three things, then. Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
Nope, no allergies that I know of. I've taken everything.
Good. Now, I'll read your numbers. Hold still for a second.
Temperature is 37.1 °C, and pulse is 76. Both nice and calm.
That's good, right? I felt awful this morning.
Numbers are a snapshot. Like checking a car's dashboard at a red light, it doesn't tell you what the engine did yesterday.
Ha, okay. So what do you think is going on?
Honestly, I can't say yet. It could be strep that keeps getting a foothold, and I can't rule that out. It might also be something viral that's lingering.
So it's not just me being run down?
Being run down helps these things along, but let's not guess. I'd like to do a throat swab for strep today, that's quick.
Is that the gagging one?
Afraid so. Two seconds and a bit of an awkward face, then it's over.
Great. I'll try to look dignified.
And I'd also like to order a blood test to check for mono, since the glands have been swollen so long.
Mono? Like, the kissing disease? I'm forty-one.
It's not only for teenagers. Plenty of adults get it, and it can drag on for weeks, which would fit your story.
Okay. Blood draw, that's fine. When do I find out?
Swab result in a day or two, bloods a bit longer. The front desk will call you.
Okay. And what do I do about the throat in the meantime?
Warm salt water, plenty of fluids, and rest. Your throat is like a sprained ankle. It heals faster if you stop walking on it.
That's hard. It's a busy week coming up.
Then take as many quiet minutes as you can steal. Even small breaks help.
Fine. I'll sneak some in at lunch.
I'd like to see you again in one week, to go through the results together.
One week. Okay, I'll book it at the desk.
Good. And keep the Tylenol at the dose you're using, don't push past it.
Right, I won't.
Anything else bugging you today?
Just the parking validation, I forgot to bring the ticket. Never mind.
The front desk can stamp it for you on the way out.
Sounds good. Thanks, doc.
You're welcome. Go see the nurse for the swab on your way out.
Will do. Bye.
